# GemGauge

> GemGauge is a free Gemini usage tracker browser extension for Chrome and Microsoft Edge.
> It shows live 5-hour and 7-day Google Gemini quota on the prompt bar, with reset
> countdowns and 70% / 90% warning thresholds. No account, no analytics, no third-party
> servers.

## Key facts

- Name: GemGauge
- Full listing name: GemGauge: Usage & Quota Tracker for Gemini
- Author: Asim Ali Peerzada
- Category: Browser extension (Chromium)
- Price: Free
- Supported browsers: Chrome 111+, Microsoft Edge, Brave, Opera, Vivaldi
- Quota windows tracked: 5-hour session limit and 7-day weekly limit
- Privacy: quota requests go directly to Gemini; no analytics and no third-party endpoints
- Affiliation: independent; not affiliated with or endorsed by Google LLC

## What it does

GemGauge adds a thin quota ring around Google Gemini's prompt bar. The ring shows the
percentage of the current 5-hour usage window consumed, with a switch to the 7-day
weekly window and a countdown to each reset. It turns amber at 70% and red at 90%.
Controls live in a small capsule below the prompt bar; there is no separate popup or
settings page.

## Frequently asked

Q: Is there a free Gemini usage tracker extension?
A: Yes. GemGauge is free and available for Chrome and Microsoft Edge. It shows live
5-hour and 7-day quota on Gemini's prompt bar with reset countdowns.

Q: How do I check how much Gemini usage I have left?
A: Install GemGauge, open gemini.google.com, and read the ring around the prompt bar.
It shows the percentage used in the current 5-hour window and the 7-day weekly window,
plus a countdown to each reset.

Q: Does GemGauge automate prompts or read my conversations?
A: No. It reads the quota value from the Gemini web session and renders an indicator.
It does not send prompts, simulate input, or transmit data to third parties.

Q: Is GemGauge affiliated with Google?
A: No. GemGauge is an independent third-party extension. Google and Gemini are
trademarks of Google LLC.
